title: Impact of Higher Interest Rates on Residential and Commercial Mortgagee Listings, and on Bankruptcy Applications
what_it_is: Impact of Higher Interest Rates on Residential and Commercial Mortgagee Listings, and on Bankruptcy Applications

sections.label: Bankruptcy and mortgagee listings
sections.summary: Bankruptcy applications could rise as vulnerable borrowers face higher rates and slower growth, with Q1 2023 foreclosures at five commercial and five residential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether the Government is anticipating a further rise in bankruptcy applications in 2023; and (b) whether residential and commercial mortgagee listings are at risk of rising further amid higher interest rates and a tougher business climate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This is slightly higher than the average quarterly bankruptcy applications of 912 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Bankruptcy applications could pick up further, as a small segment of more vulnerable borrowers face higher risks of financial distress amid higher interest rates and slower economic growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Five commercial and five residential loans were foreclosed by financial institutions (FIs) in the first quarter of 2023, compared to an average of four commercial and 12 residential foreclosures per quarter in 2022.

sections.label: Residents seeking mortgage help
sections.summary: Residents seek help with financial institutions on mortgages; MAS said 27,000 homeowners refinanced in the past 12 months, with average payment increase around $240.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am seeing some residents coming up to me to seek help with FIs in regard to their mortgages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I think the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) just replied to me yesterday on my written Parliamentary Question, that 27,000 home owners have refinanced in the past 12 months and also indicated that MAS estimates that an increase in mortgage payments for these home borrowers was around $240 on average.

sections.label: Floating rate mortgage share
sections.summary: About 38% of private residential mortgages by financial institutions were floating rate as of Q1 2023, and the $240 average was about 2% of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As of the first quarter of 2023, about 38% of mortgages extended for private residential property purchases by FIs were on floating rate packages that move in tandem with market interest rates, while the remaining 62% were either on rates linked to board rates or fixed deposit rates, which track market interest rates but with some lag or it could be fixed interest rates over the first few years of their loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With regards to the written Parliamentary Question yesterday, the "$240 on average" accounts for about 2% of their monthly income and the average monthly income of the 27,000 homeowners who refinanced their loans had increased by about 10%.

sections.label: Example of payment increase
sections.summary: Borrowers last refinanced in February 2020 at about 1.8% faced an average monthly payment increase of about $730 after refinancing in February 2023 at about 3.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: An example of an upper bound that I can share with the Member, borrowers whose loans were incepted, or at least last refinanced in February 2020 at the interest rate of about 1.8%, faced an average increase in monthly payment of about $730 or about 6% as a share of monthly income after refinancing in February 2023 at an interest rate about 3.9%.

sections.label: MAS borrowing limit measures
sections.summary: MAS has put in place measures to limit property borrowing, including the Total Debt Servicing Ratio, which applies to residential and commercial property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I just wanted to give the Member that context on mortgage listings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That said, may I take this opportunity to also share and remind Members that MAS has put in place, over the years, measures to limit the amount one can borrow to buy property, including the Total Debt Servicing Ratio, which applies to both residential as well as commercial property.
